title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Platform
description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. title: Software Engineer, New Grad
description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works. Your role Stripe is large enough that individual products and projects can be rapidly deployed to a meaningful fraction of the world’s businesses, but small enough that individual agency still has outsized impact. Small teams can impact how millions of businesses grow. Right now the global economy is replatforming around AI, creating new opportunities for growth. We’re at the center of this, and we think the best work is still in front of us. To meet this moment, we’re looking for people who move with urgency, like hard problems, and want their work to matter at a time of great change. If that’s you, there’s no better place to build your career. Who you are Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty. Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus. Minimum requirements A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science or a directly related field, obtained by summer 2027, or equivalent work experience; New grad candidates should have no more than 18 months of professional experience (excluding internship experience). Experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Java, Ruby, JavaScript, Scala, and Go. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present. Experience from either previous internships or working collaboratively on multi-person coding projects (in a university or professional setting). Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor or subject matter experts. Clear written communication skills, with the ability to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes. Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs. Preferred qualifications One or more areas of specialized knowledge (frontend, backend, infrastructure or other technologies) balanced with general skills and knowledge. Experience in code review practices, and an understanding of how to safely update production systems. Familiarity with navigating and managing work in large code bases. Experience leading small projects independently, and contributing to larger projects alongside peers. Ability to operate with high agency in navigating complex technical obstacles independently, knowing precisely when to unblock oneself and when to ask for help.

The Difference You Will Make: You will manage Airbnb.org’s emergency responses in the APAC region but will also be expected to support responses globally as required. You will monitor disasters around the world, decide with your manager when an event meets our activation criteria, stand the response up, and manage it through to close-out. You will do this work with partners on the ground. Local nonprofits and agencies find displaced people, confirm eligibility, and provide case management. Your job is to make sure those partners are ready before an event, and that during one they have the housing supply, the guidance, and the answers they need. Speed matters, and so does the quality of the placement. You will run several responses at the same time, in different countries and at different stages. You will keep internal teams and external partners informed before they have to ask. You will work across Operations, Strategic Partnerships, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Finance, and Product to deliver one coordinated response. Experience in Social Impact for tech companies is a big plus. Much of the work is not defined in advance. You will need to set direction yourself, decide with incomplete information, and move things toward clarity and action. You must also be able to deploy to the field on short notice to manage disaster response programs on the ground if needed. Establish, activate, and oversee emergency housing responses in close collaboration with on-the-ground partners responsible for the intake and case management of individuals displaced by disasters. Proactively communicate status, decisions, and next steps to internal and external cross-functional stakeholders and partners. Manage each response end-to-end: verify partner readiness, determine response size and stay lengths, launch operations, monitor placements, solve issues, and conclude based on clear exit criteria. Manage partnerships (including onboarding new partners and managing existing partners) during active emergencies, and ensuring smooth handoff to the Partnerships team at the conclusion of emergency responses. Promptly answer partner questions during live responses, escalating unresolved ones. Work closely with the Partnerships team to build and manage partnerships with organizations that vet and support guests, while working with our Operations team to optimize housing supply, reduce costs, and maximize positive impact for those affected. Collaborate with the Strategic Partnerships team to unify efforts and amplify our reach in response to major disasters. Enhance operational readiness during non-crisis periods. Sharpen activation criteria and playbooks, pre-position partner agreements, expand 24/7 global coverage, increase team capacity, and advocate for the product features the operation needs. Integrate best practices from experts and agencies, and cultivate relationships with government bodies and emergency management authorities in key regions before an event happens. Deploy to disaster zones on short notice to manage ground operations, and hand over cleanly when you leave. Write the after-action review for each response, and make sure the changes it calls for actually happen. Direct experience activating and running disaster responses end to end. Experience working in Social Impact at tech companies is a big plus. title: SDE2 - API Platform

title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
description:
THE ROLE

Sarvam's products produce events, model traces, evals and billing data, and need to read that data back. The Data Platform team builds and runs the central data infrastructure every product uses: ingestion, streaming, the analytical warehouse, transformations, access control and audit.

We are hiring a Software Engineer / Senior Software Engineer (2–5 years of experience) to own this platform end to end. You will design, build and run systems that other teams depend on in production, and make real decisions on database internals, streaming and platform design. Stack: Go/Python, ClickHouse Cloud, Kafka, Avro, Airflow, dbt, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DO

 - Build and run the ingestion path: the service every product sends events to, Kafka behind it, and the pipes that land data in ClickHouse within seconds. Own schema validation, rate limits, dead-letter handling and the client SDKs.

 - Own the warehouse: ClickHouse Cloud. Design tables for the read path (sorting keys, partitions, materialized views, TTL), separate compute per workload, set per-user limits and per-tenant isolation, and attribute cost to the team that spent it.

 - Build reliable data pipelines and solve data problems: dbt models and Airflow DAGs with the BI engineers, CDC from product databases, sync and backfill jobs that are safe to re-run, and the data problems product teams bring you, such as a late source, a number that doesn't match or a query that has slowed down.

 - Make the platform self-serve: a registry of every dataset with its owner, schema, freshness and access; provisioning and permissions as code.

 - Run it in production: everything as Terraform and Helm with metrics, traces and alerts; be on call; handle incidents end to end, write the RCA and fix the root cause.

 - Grow the platform: new products keep arriving. You will help decide what the platform should do next and build it, whether that is a new source or sink, or a new way for teams to use the data.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2–5 years of experience building, shipping and running large-scale, data-intensive systems in production, ideally at a startup where you owned things and were on call for them.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of: an OLAP database (ClickHouse preferred; Druid, BigQuery or Redshift also fine) or Kafka / event streaming. You understand how a columnar store writes, merges and scans data, or how a partitioned log gives ordering and delivery guarantees.

 - Experience with large-scale messaging systems like Kafka or RabbitMQ: partitions, consumer groups, delivery guarantees, backpressure.

 - Good at Go, or good at Python.

 - You know the usual data-system problems: schema evolution, idempotency, backpressure, partitioning, retention and TTL, CDC.

 - You have built or run at least one of: an event pipeline, a transformation layer (dbt, Spark or SQL on Airflow), a provisioning or control-plane service, or a multi-tenant data service with access control.

 - Comfortable with AWS, Kubernetes and Terraform in production.

 - You test before shipping, debug with metrics and traces, write RCAs, and document what you build.

 - Passion for data infrastructure and for enabling others by making their data easier to access.


NICE TO HAVE

 - ClickHouse in production: MergeTree, materialized views, projections, quotas, settings profiles, row policies, ClickHouse Cloud.

 - Kafka in depth: MSK, Kafka Connect, schema registry (Glue or Confluent), Avro.

description: Data Scientist/ML Job Summary Photon is hiring an experienced Data Scientist / Machine Learning Engineer, to design, build, validate, and operationalize a closed-loop Propensity-to-Pay model for Enercare Collections. The engagement runs on Enercares existing Azure platform (Azure Data Factory, ADLS, Azure Machine Learning, and Azure SQL) and reuses current ingestion and CDS integration patterns. The role owns one primary Collections model: define the pay target and scoring population, engineer features from customer, account, payment, AR, invoice, usage, delinquency, write-off, and collections history, rank accounts by likelihood to pay, and assign agreed risk segments. Scores are produced on a scheduled batch cycle, with model version and evaluation details published for CDS. Outcome and treatment feedback are brought back so cycle-over-cycle performance can show when the model should be retrained. This is a hands-on delivery role. The hire is expected to contribute from Discovery and to take the model through validation, UAT, production scoring, and handover with in agreed timeline with customer. Key Responsibilities Work with Collections business owners and data owners during Discovery to confirm the scoring population, the definition of “pay,” the prediction horizon, label history, success metrics, and acceptance thresholds. Assess whether available history, quality, and coverage can support a viable model, and document limitations, assumptions, and the baseline comparison against the current Collections prioritisation process. Define and build payment, AR, billing, customer, usage, delinquency, write-off, and collections behavioural features from the consolidated analytical dataset. Freeze the feature list with the data science lead and business owner before model build. Build and train one primary Propensity-to-Pay model, including target construction, feature selection, training, scoring, and tuning against agreed metrics. Validate technically and with the business: scoring completeness, data-leakage controls, reproducibility, output consistency, ranking and segment behaviour, calibration, and lift versus the agreed Collections baseline. Convert scores into risk segments using agreed thresholds, retain the model segment when an authorized business override is applied, and support treatment/action mapping defined by Collections. Produce a model card, validation evidence, and a reviewable scored sample for stakeholder sign-off. Implement model governance on Azure Machine Learning: unique model version identifiers, evaluation results, visibility of which version is deployed in each environment, and which version produced each scoring output. Support an alternate-version path so a candidate model can be tested in the operations layer before approval, and support controlled rollback to the previous approved version. Operationalize scheduled batch scoring with feature refresh, score generation, and controls that publish only complete, validated score sets. Failed runs must leave the last valid published scores in place. Design the closed loop: capture operational feedback and actual pay outcomes, compare performance across cycles, and recommend when retraining is required. Document what would be needed for later automated retraining; implementation beyond the agreed Collections scope is a separate change. Collaborate with data engineers on ADF, ADLS, and Azure SQL pipelines, and with QA on reconciliation of counts, score distribution, segments, and CDS output fields (customer/account key, propensity score, segment, model version, evaluation date). Use Enercare’s Azure DevOps promotion path across Development/QA, UAT, and Production. Support UAT, defect resolution, hypercare, runbook handover, and knowledge transfer. Document features, experiments, metrics, thresholds, overrides, and operating guidance so Enercare operations can run a production scoring cycle with guidance. Required Skills and Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a related field. 5–8 years in data science or machine learning, including at least one classification or ranking model taken through batch scoring in production. title: Machine Learning Engineer, Robotic Foundation Models
description: About PhyAgentsPhyAgents is a high-growth foundation model startup headquartered in San Jose, California. Founded by Stanford alumni, it sits at the intersection of the two biggest platform shifts of our time: foundation models and robotics. It delivers semi-humanoid robots as a workforce for industrial applications.Their “physical agents” (or robots) combine a robotic foundation model, force-aware manipulation, long-horizon reasoning, step-by-step execution verified against real operating procedures, and human-in-the-loop autonomy. The robot plans the job, executes each step, checks their work, and when it isn’t certain it doesn't guess—it escalates.About The TeamCEO and co-founder: Serial entrepreneur and former VP at Intel. Previously raised >$50M, scaled and exited a robotics company. PhD from Stanford.CTO and co-founder: Key foundation models leader from Apple. Previously led perception for self-driving. MS from Stanford, B.Tech from IIT Madras.The team includes executives and AI leaders from Apple, Intel, Marvell, Samsung, Uber, Panasonic, VMWare and Lockheed Martin.Why join nowYou’ll be among the first engineers in the India team of a Silicon Valley deep tech startup. You’ll work on the same problems, with the same bar, as our team in San Jose. This is not a satellite office working off tickets. That gap is the company. Closing it takes models that learn from demonstration and improve through practice, a data flywheel that turns every failure into training signal, and software that runs on real robots in real industrial environments.About The RoleAt PhyAgents, a machine learning engineer works across the full loop that makes a robot better: data, models, training, simulation, evaluation, and deployment on real hardware. You’ll do research-grade work and ship it onto robots in the same quarter. A result that doesn’t run on the robot isn’t finished.What You Will Work OnTraining and post-training: Train and post-train robotic foundation models, including vision-language-action models, using imitation learning and reinforcement learning. Train policies with reinforcement learning that transfer to real robots.Rewards and verifiers: Design the reward functions and the verifiers that check whether a task step actually succeeded.Evaluation: Build harnesses that tell us whether a model actually got better, in simulation and on real hardware. Design the metrics that decide what ships.Data and data infrastructure: Define what data the models need. Build the pipelines that turn raw robot episodes into versioned, training-ready datasets. Trace a stuck policy back to its data.Models on robots: Get models running reliably and fast enough on real hardware. You finish things. A result that doesn’t run on the robot isn’t finished.Rigor. You catch the subtle bug that the dashboard says is fine.Range. You’re as willing to debug a data pipeline or a ROS node as a training run.Comfort with real hardware. Our models run on robots, and you’ll spend time in the lab.Speed of learning. There’s no playbook. You’ll be learning new parts of the stack every month.Ambition. You want to build something that matters at the frontier of AI and robotics.Clear communication. You’ll work daily across San Jose, Bengaluru, and our data operations team in Nepal.
